criteria.criterion: set_tree_writable in snapshot.rs treats an entry that disappears between read_dir and stat/chmod (io NotFound) as already handled, instead of returning an error; other errors still propagate.
criteria.evidence: snapshot.rs:270-275: walk_tree_writable maps Err(GitError::Spawn(e)) with e.kind()==NotFound to Ok(()) and returns every other result unchanged. walk_one (lines 277-299) collects read_dir's entries first, then recurses through walk_tree_writable for each one, so a vanished child is skipped and the walk goes on. Errors other than NotFound still reach the caller through `?`.

criteria.criterion: A regression test in snapshot.rs shows the cause: a walk over a tree where an entry is removed mid-walk (or an equivalent deterministic simulation) succeeds, rather than relying on timing.
criteria.evidence: New test a_walk_survives_entries_removed_after_the_directory_was_listed (snapshot.rs ~569-590). Its `between` hook deletes files and directory b after the parent is listed and before each child is examined. It asserts the walk succeeds, that at least 3 entries were removed, and that walking a missing path returns Ok. Without the NotFound handling, symlink_metadata on a removed child would return Err and unwrap() would panic, so the test catches the regression. It passed in every run.

criteria.criterion: Git commands run in snapshots no longer start background gc/maintenance (e.g. gc.auto=0, maintenance.auto=false), with the reasoning commented, if the producer confirms this is a source of the vanishing files.
criteria.evidence: lib.rs:177-181: Git::isolated, which the doc comment says is used for snapshots, adds gc.auto=0, gc.autoDetach=false and maintenance.auto=false, with a comment explaining that detached gc or maintenance creates and removes files under .git. The producer did not reproduce the race (the CHANGELOG says so) but added the settings as a complementary measure, which the reading allows.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git` (including a_locked_snapshot_refuses_edits_and_commits_and_keeps_head_and_tree) and it passes; the tests repeat passing across several runs.
criteria.evidence: In the snapshot: 3 full runs of `cargo test -p athena-git` passed 28/28, and the verbose run listed a_locked_snapshot_refuses_edits_and_commits_and_keeps_head_and_tree ... ok. The snapshot-test filter passed 8/8, and the flaky test alone passed 1/1.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Clippy finished with no warnings; `cargo fmt --check` printed nothing.

findings.summary: A NotFound error on the walk's root path is now swallowed too, so Snapshot::lock() on a snapshot directory that does not exist returns Ok instead of an error.
findings.evidence: walk_tree_writable is also applied to the top-level path that set_tree_writable is called with, and the new test asserts that a missing path returns Ok. In lock(), when the directory is missing both write probes fail, so probe_write returns None and lock() returns Ok(()). Before this change, lock() returned a NotFound error. Suggested fix: only tolerate NotFound for children, not for the root path.

summary: The change fixes the cause the reading names. In snapshot.rs, set_tree_writable now lists each directory's entries before touching any of them. A NotFound error on an entry that vanishes during the walk (from stat, read_dir or chmod) is treated as already handled, and every other error still propagates. In lib.rs, Git::isolated now sets gc.auto=0, gc.autoDetach=false and maintenance.auto=false, with a comment saying why. A new test (a_walk_survives_entries_removed_after_the_directory_was_listed) uses a hook to delete entries after their directory is listed, so it does not depend on timing. It would fail if the NotFound handling were removed. The CHANGELOG entry names the cause and says honestly that the race was not reproduced. In my snapshot, `cargo test -p athena-git` passed 3 times as a full run (28/28), plus one run of the snapshot tests and one run of the flaky test alone. Clippy on the workspace and `cargo fmt --check` were both clean. All three changed files are on the deliverables list. One minor issue: lock() on a snapshot directory that does not exist now returns Ok instead of an error.
